title: AI access
lede: Assistants such as ChatGPT or Claude that you connected to Recreatio (MCP) read the areas of their connection — only read, and only the Library, Scriptorium and knowledge bases. Add, renew or remove areas here.
manageHint: Already connected an assistant? Add this area to its connection without signing in again:
connectLater: You can add more areas to this connection later, without connecting again:
unlockWhy: Access links open only on your device — enter your password.
none: No assistant is connected yet. In ChatGPT or Claude, add a custom MCP server with the address above and OAuth; Recreatio then asks you which areas it may read. After that, its connection appears here and you can add more areas.
older: Connections made before 5 November 2026 keep working with the areas chosen back then, but they are not listed here and cannot be extended. Reconnect such an assistant once; from then on you add areas here.

how.title: How it works
how.noReconnect: Adding, renewing or removing an area needs no new sign-in: the assistant sees the change at its next call (list_collections).
how.reconnect: Sign in again from the assistant only for a new assistant, an older connection, or a connection that was revoked or has expired.
how.readOnly: Always read-only: the assistant can search and read the collections of its areas. It cannot change anything and never sees learner progress, answers, chats, forms or calendars.

connection.noAreas: This connection reads no area right now. Add one — the assistant stays connected.

statusHelp.expired: The access link of this area has expired. Renew it, and the assistant reads it again.
statusHelp.pending: The access link of this area was never finished. Remove the area and add it again.
statusHelp.notLeader: You no longer lead this area, so this connection does not read it.
statusHelp.creatorLeft: The person who made this access link no longer leads the area. Remove the area and add it again — a new link is made.

area.whole: Whole area — collections created later are included.

remove.body: The assistant stops reading this area at its next call. Other areas stay connected, and the area's access link itself is kept.

revoke.body: The assistant loses access to every area of this connection at its next call. The areas' access links are kept. To connect it again, sign in from the assistant.

snap.liturgy: Liturgy: canonical works, editions, texts, passages, observances, templates, assignments and explicit rules. Stable canonical IDs are in data.id; references name resources, never copied daily texts. Drafts and missing dependencies are not approved liturgical content.
snap.base:
## Knowledge base entries (Cogita)
An entry has kinds ("kinds" — the first gives the name) and fields in "data" according to its kinds; what each field means — in "kinds" of this collection.
Field types: {types}.
A value may be uncertain: {"value", "state", "source": {"work": work id, "locator": "p. 23"}, "note"}; states: {states}.
A reference is the id of another entry (with its title in the entry's "refs"); a reference with a place: {"value": id, "locator": "Ps 110"}.
The field "blocks" is a statement: paragraphs {"type": "paragraph", "text"}, lists {"type": "ordered"|"unordered", "items"}, tables {"type": "table", "columns", "rows"}; a cell is a list of pieces {"text"} or {"ref": id, "locator"}. Thesis = the first sentence of the first paragraph.
Question: one kind "question"; "form" (question type) says how it asks: {questions}; a field with "when" belongs only to the given question types; "about" — entries the question tests; "needs" — what must be known before it.
Learning order: a reference field with "prerequisite": "up" — what it points to must be known EARLIER (concept → “Requires”); "down" — the entries pointed to build on this. From such fields the app computes levels from the basics (level 1 — nothing before it) and asks the general first, then the detailed.
Dates: "1999", "1999-05", "1999-05-03", "-1000" (BC); range: {"segments": [{"from", "to"}]}.
Structure (e.g. the argument of an article): a reference field with "structure": "up" — this entry lies UNDER what it points to (a step under a question, a reply under an objection); "structure": "down" — the entries pointed to lie under it. The root (no value in the "up" field) is usually the leading question. Its tree: via MCP get_related(root id, direction "in", fields: [key of the "up" field], depth 3), then again from every entry at depth 3 (at most 60 entries per call; with "truncated" the edges also name those that didn't fit — continue from them); via REST /entry/{id}: entries in "linkedFrom" with this field lie directly below — and so on from each of them (or, looking through all entries: under entry X lie those whose "up" field has value X). The order of steps is the order of their places in the work (a reference field with a place in a work from the library). Entries pointing to a step through a field without "structure" (e.g. a comment: "About") don't belong to the reconstruction — they are others' or own remarks.
